column2: Bloom and Drigil put assistance inside a daily care or work routine, while Tribune connects policy changes to public input. The projects show an assistant doing a specific job for a specific audience.
Guardian and Tend help people understand a financial claim, while Settlr helps roommates coordinate moving expenses. Each gives a person a decision to make with the result.
Silent Voice applies speech synthesis to communication after voice loss, and SpeakEasy uses it for pronunciation practice. Both give the user an audible result to evaluate.
CrisisLens, Data Saves Lives, and Bin-It turn raw data into a ranked list or map someone can use to decide where help is needed.
A-Eye and HUDson use audio in accessibility workflows. Incantation and CodeCrack use voice input as part of the main interaction, for casting spells or answering interview questions.
Farsight, Dronautics, and Doorway all collect signals from a physical space and turn them into something an operator can use.
Fish Market coordinates buyers and sellers, while HAVEN connects building signals to evacuation planning. Both give agents roles in a workflow and a result a person can inspect.
Accent and BraceML give users immediate feedback in the interface. Two Figma made the interaction itself the build by implementing a design tool inside Figma.
Farsight turns a physical rover run into a room someone can explore in VR. It makes the simulation part of the same demo as the hardware.
The projects span robotics, classroom support, and shopping. Their common link is the domain-name prize, which appears across different kinds of builds.
Playwright turns a script into visual previews, and ListenMe suggests a word from a spoken description. Both start from a concrete input a judge can try.
AERIS, Jade.AI, and Navi bring model output into a response, data, or browsing workflow where someone can act on it.
Farsight, Permanence, and Here connect model output to the physical world through person detection, object tracking, or sound awareness.
GroundTruth, Eve, and Backrooms apply automation to a defined operations or finance task such as disputes, event accounting, or back-office work.
MovieMind finds matching reviews, and Munchkin classifies incoming files. Both organize a collection and use it to make a recommendation.
The projects range from research to health and group planning. DrugPersona and Homie both help someone move through a process with several steps and decisions.
Fireline, Farsight, and TORQ run perception or control at the device. Each gives judges a physical input and a response they can observe.
Mira, Fable, and ContainOS feed scene, sensor, or model information into an output that changes as the situation changes.
UnderPressure changes a game in response to the player's state, while VibeSense converts facial cues into audio. In both, a sensed signal changes the experience.
Pixel Truth and Inbox Invaders put an online safety lesson inside a game where players act on it. Mindful Egg gives players a visible reward for practicing a habit.
MediSnap, SnapChest, and Ghostface Cookah let people use hands-free information or feedback while their attention stays on a real task.
Vigil and Waste2Taste collect repeated observations and turn them into a decision about what to check or change.
No Badge Actors, solGPU, and VERA tie a transaction to a task someone already understands, such as checking a recipient or booking compute.
Rally, CoClip, and Pacioli use shared state for a live interaction between people, whether it is a game, a video edit, or an accounting canvas.
Hakit combines teammate assignments with live GitHub progress in one view so the team can see what still needs work.
FlameScout, Spotlight, and Nexus collect signals from several sources and present them in a workspace for a particular operator.
Arena, CodeAncestry, and stackwise solve specific developer tasks such as comparing implementations, understanding old decisions, and scaffolding a project.
